conventions.convention: The horizon T is finite and may be zero; state and observation dimensions are positive integers. The empty observation history is a singleton.
Initial, process, measurement, predicted-state, and filtered-state covariances may be singular positive-semidefinite matrices; every innovation covariance solved must be positive definite.
Conditional laws are everywhere-defined probability-kernel versions satisfying conditional event identities; no pointwise uniqueness on null observation histories is asserted.
The gain is computed by factoring S = LLᵀ and solving LU = HP followed by LᵀKᵀ = U, column by column.
AC is assumed for the Gaussian-law and conditional-law suppliers. Initial state and all process and measurement noises are mutually independent.
Independent-noise extension requires the new noise Z to be independent of the pair (X,Y), and assumes a supplied conditional law of X given Y; arbitrary measurable target spaces are allowed.

load_bearing.statement: Under AC, the finite-horizon independent-noise linear-Gaussian model with positive-semidefinite covariances and positive-definite innovation covariances has the everywhere-defined filtering-kernel version π_k(y₁:ₖ,·) = N(mₖ|ₖ(y₁:ₖ),Pₖ|ₖ) returned by alg-kalman-filter, for every 0 ≤ k ≤ T. Each updated covariance is positive semidefinite and admits the Joseph expression.

If Z is independent of (X,Y) and κ is a supplied conditional law of X given Y, then Λ(h,·) = κ(h,·) ⊗ L(Z) is a conditional law of (X,Z) given Y. Its pushforward through any measurable Φ is a conditional law of Φ(X,Z) given Y.

Assume AC and positive dimensions. For mutually independent Gaussian U, q, r with positive-semidefinite covariances, X = FU + q and Y = HX + r have the displayed joint Gaussian block covariance. If S = H(FPFᵀ + Q)Hᵀ + R is positive definite, the conditional law of X given Y has the Kalman mean and covariance for every observation value; the covariance is positive semidefinite and equals the Joseph expression.

For an admissible finite independent-noise linear-Gaussian model, initialize the supplied mean and covariance, then predict, form the innovation covariance, compute the gain using Cholesky triangular solves, and update the mean and covariance for k = 1,…,T. For T = 0 return the initial pair.

Product probabilities, rectangle formulas, and iterated section integrals.
Finite positive dimensions, PSD covariance inputs, AC, and mutual independence of initial state and noises.
Operational meaning of the gain's triangular solves.

Correctness and uniqueness of columnwise triangular gain solves; no complexity conclusion is imported.

seams_checked.note: The exactness theorem uses the filtering-kernel definition and finite-horizon existence result with AC, standard-Borel spaces, singleton empty history, and conditional-version qualifications intact. It proves the Gaussian recursion locally rather than importing the dominated recursion.

The one-step lemma and exactness theorem apply Gaussian conditioning with PSD joint covariance, positive dimensions, AC, and SPD observed innovation block. Singular state and conditional covariances remain allowed; no singular-observed-block extension is inferred.

The backward-kernel lemma, RTS algorithm, and RTS theorem retain forward innovation admissibility and conditional-version semantics. They separately require SPD forecast covariance for backward solves and do not attribute that stronger assumption to the filter.

The conditional-path lemma fixes a nonlinear path, obtaining deterministic linear-Gaussian coefficients and independent Gaussian noises. Its SPD measurement covariance ensures SPD innovations. The RBPF uses exact Gaussian components while retaining a finite-particle approximation for the nonlinear path and finite-positive evidence conditions.
